validity.researcher_notes: This is SoCalGas's whole intrastate gas transmission system (not a single certificated project) serving Southern California. Existence and classification confirmed independently: SoCalGas's own site (socalgas.com/stay-safe/pipeline-and-storage-safety/natural-gas-transmission) describes 'SoCalGas owns and operates an integrated gas transmission system' spanning from the Colorado River (east) to the Pacific Coast (west), Tulare County (north) to the US/Mexico border (south) -- entirely within California; the CPUC's own Summer 2021 Southern California Gas Reliability Assessment (state regulator, May 2021, independent of SoCalGas) corroborates the same system as a live, operating gas transmission network with three major transmission zones (Northern, Southern, Wheeler Ridge). SoCalGas's FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-02-26, as of 12/31/2025) confirms the entity is real, currently operating, and correctly classed a natural gas transmission (not distribution-only or gathering) system: 'SoCalGas' natural gas facilities included 52,765 miles of distribution pipelines, 3,030 miles of transmission and storage pipelines, 48,900 miles of service pipelines and seven transmission compressor stations.' No duplicate risk against the roster -- P6250 (PG&E) and (elsewhere) SDG&E are separate California utility systems with their own rows. Caveats filed separately below: (1) the recorded Capacity (3,725 MMcf/d) is a pipeline+storage COMBINED figure per its own cited source, not pipeline capacity alone; (2) the recorded Length (3,640 mi) is corroborated by its own 2013 cited source but conflicts with two more recent, independent mileage figures (a 2022 CPUC compliance filing and the FY2025 SEC 10-K), suggesting the sheet's mileage may be stale; (3) StartState/Province carries a trailing whitespace typo.

validity.recommendation: Verify whether Capacity should record pipeline-only deliverability rather than the combined pipeline+storage figure currently cited.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Capacity (3,725 MMcf/d) is stated verbatim in its own cited source (CPUC Summer 2021 Southern California Gas Reliability Assessment, p.2), but that document is explicit that the number is NOT pipeline capacity alone: 'Pipeline and storage capacity combined can provide 3,725 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd) of natural gas' (emphasis added -- executive summary). The same document's Table 4 (Transmission Zone Assumed Operational Capacities) sums the system's three named transmission zones (Northern 870 + Wheeler Ridge 765 + Southern 670 MMcfd, plus a minor Line 85 Zone of 60 MMcfd) to roughly 2,365 MMcfd of pipeline-only inbound capacity for summer 2021 -- materially less than 3,725. So the recorded number is real and correctly quoted from its ref, but it measures a different (broader) quantity than 'pipeline capacity' as the GEM Capacity field intends. Recommend a researcher confirm the pipeline-only transmission capacity (candidate figure ~2,365 MMcfd per Table 4, though that is a single reliability-assessment snapshot, not a nameplate/certificated rating) before treating 3,725 as the pipeline's own capacity. Not overriding the value here since no single authoritative pipeline-only nameplate capacity figure was found within this pass's search budget (WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-sweep).

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's LengthKnown (3,640 mi) is stated verbatim in its own cited ref (SoCalGas 'Pipeline Classifications' fact sheet, dated January 2013, citing 'Summer 2011' data: 'our 3,640-mile transmission pipeline system'). Two more recent, independently-dated documents give different, lower mileage for the same system: (1) SoCalGas's 2022 CPUC compliance filing (Rulemaking R.15-01-008, June 2022 report, Appendix 1 -- transmission-pipeline leak data by pipe material) lists two pipe-material rows for 'SoCalGas Transmission Territory' totaling 3,440 mi (1 mi 'PB' + 3,439 mi 'PC') for 2021; (2) SoCalGas's FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-02-26, as of 12/31/2025) states 'SoCalGas' natural gas facilities included ... 3,030 miles of transmission and storage pipelines' (note: that figure bundles transmission with storage-field piping, so it is not a clean apples-to-apples comparison to the sheet's transmission-only 3,640 mi). All three figures name the same SoCalGas system and are dated (2011-vintage, 2021-vintage, 2025-vintage respectively) but disagree by hundreds of miles, and the trend is downward over time -- consistent with either genuine retirement/consolidation of transmission mileage or a reclassification of some transmission mileage into distribution/storage categories over the intervening decade. Not proposing a replacement value here because the three sources are not measuring identical scopes (transmission-only vs. transmission+storage) and a merge-time researcher should reconcile which of the CPUC 2022 (3,440 mi, transmission-only, closest in scope to the sheet's definition) or a newer regulatory filing is the best current figure.
